summary: All nine pairs ran in the same sandbox, which denied cmake and any shell command containing the literal EXERCISM_RUN_ALL_TESTS. So every run had to either find a workaround (-include header, split string) or ship unverified code, and several passing runs (P02 r2, P05 r1, P07 r2, P08 r2, P09 r1) also shipped unverified and simply had correct code. Six failures (P03, P04, P06, P07, P08, P09) are ordinary unverified-completion mistakes: a missing conversion overload, a const distribution, int overflow, an unconditional write, an inverted loop condition, a missing include. Some of these also overclaim 'compiles clean' or show hand traces that follow the intended code rather than the written code (most visibly P06). Two failures differ in kind: P02 run 1 and P05 run 2 had correct code but fell into long verbatim cycles of identical reasoning text and identical no-op or denied tool calls until the harness stopped them, which looks like degenerate generation rather than a normal agent error. P01 run 1 sits between the two groups: a probable iterator runaway (grade 'oom') that the agent misattributed to the OS for the rest of the session, with some stale repeated reasoning.
